rows.name: SourceHut
rows.reason: SourceHut hosts Git, tickets, virtualized builds and email patch review. Service remains public alpha; builds require payment, and contributor workflow changes need evaluation.

rows.name: GitLab.com
rows.reason: Hosted GitHub importer and separate Actions-to-CI migration path. Import permissions/data limits apply; organizations excluded, CI requires conversion. Comparative availability advantage and project-specific price unestablished.

rows.name: soft-serve
rows.reason: Self-hosted Git fits; smaller collaboration scope/self-hosting aren't prohibited. Archived 2026-10-26 with security updates ended; later caveats cannot establish earlier violation of an unstated maintenance requirement.

rows.name: Gitea repository mirroring
rows.reason: Gitea schedules pull/push mirrors of Git history for staged migration. It does not provide full workflow failover; synchronization can lag and push mirrors overwrite remote changes.

rows.name: Codeberg
rows.reason: Hosted code forge eligibility depends on fit with its free-software mission, which is unspecified. No stated private-commercial-hosting requirement supplies a violation.

rows.name: Self-hosted Forgejo
rows.reason: Self-hosted forge provides hosting control; willingness and operational capability unspecified. Forgejo Actions v15.0 documents familiarity, not GitHub Actions compatibility; workflows require validation.

rows.name: soft-serve
rows.reason: Self-hosted SSH Git service replaces repository hosting; requires operational ownership, and its October 2026 sunsetting creates a post-cutoff maintenance caveat.

rows.name: Forgejo
rows.reason: Self-hostable Git collaboration and CI permit choosing hosting infrastructure. Operator assumes maintenance and recovery; GitHub Actions workflow compatibility is not guaranteed.

rows.name: SourceHut
rows.reason: Hosted Git, CI and email-oriented review offer another collaboration model. Contributor workflow fit unknown; service currently labeled public alpha. Migration completeness, pricing and comparative availability unverified.

rows.name: Codeberg
rows.reason: Hosted Forgejo supplies code hosting and collaboration for free-software projects; CI capacity and project eligibility need checking.

rows.name: Codeberg
rows.reason: A community-operated hosted forge is a relevant choice for qualifying free-software projects. Project eligibility is unknown. Private-content exceptions are limited; resource and CI access may need requests.

rows.name: GitBook
rows.reason: Documentation editing/publishing synchronizes with separate GitHub/GitLab repositories. That role does not replace the requested code-hosting provider; no documentation-only scope was requested.

rows.name: GitLab
rows.reason: GitLab's GitHub importer preserves substantial repository/collaboration data. Organizations do not migrate; metadata, permissions and CI need validation. No uptime advantage was established.

rows.name: GitBook
rows.reason: Documentation publishing and repository sync do not replace source-code hosting, issue tracking, and review workflows affected by GitHub outages.

rows.name: Keep GitHub with an independent Git mirror
rows.reason: An independent Git mirror preserves code access during migration assessment. Update/test it and handle LFS separately; issues/reviews/CI/releases are not covered, and stale mirrors cannot recover unreplicated work.

rows.name: Codeberg
rows.reason: Codeberg provides nonprofit Forgejo hosting and GitHub migration for free-software projects. Shared CI needs onboarding with availability/resource caveats; verify project eligibility and runner needs.
